rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING AN ADVANCED STUDIES DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR EXCEPTIONAL EMPLOYEES FROM THE GOVERNMENT AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"The Pensionado Act of 2004\". It is imperative for the government to devise a program for overseas education and training for the brightest and most promising Filipinos who are already employed or self-employed in a branch of science or technology along identified priority areas. The proposed bill endeavors to provide the country with a continuing supply of highly trained leaders for industry, research and the academe through the coordination of these talents under a single governing body where all scholarships, under foreign and local sponsorships, are pooled together.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2005-06-07, transmitted to on 2005-07-25 and received by the Senate on 2005-08-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE FORFEITURE AND DISPOSITION OF PROPERTY SEIZED BY THE BUREAU OF CUSTOMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF THE TARIFF AND CUSTOMS CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: The government's efforts to curb smuggling and other frauds have been stymied by the indiscriminate issuance of temporary retraining orders and injuctive reliefs by judicial authorities. This measure seeks to rationalize the forfeiture and disposition procedure of goods seized by the Bureau of Customs. Under the proposed bill, the Secretary of Finance, upon the recommendation of the Commissioner of Customs, shall be empowered to summarily seize smuggled goods and to sell the same.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04069

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2005-02-15
Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2005-02-22

committee_action.remarks: Substituted by HB No. 4069 (CR No. 614).  Please see HB No. 4069 for details.

rows.author: E011
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-07, transmitted to on 2006-08-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-08-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS TO UTILIZE ALL ITS INCOME FOR THEIR MAINTENANCE AND OTHER OPERATING EXPENSES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The practice of disallowing government hospitals from using their income for maintenance and other operating expenses has limited their capacity to expand and to deliver quality and efficient basic health services to the people. This bill seeks to authorize government hospitals to utilize their income from pharmacy, fees from in-house services and facilities, including but not limited to laboratory, radiology, operating room and nursery facilities; income derived form nonpatient related services such as parking fees, interview fees and tour fees, for maintenance and other operating expenditures including capital outlay.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04375

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL INSURANCE BENEFITS TO BARANGAY CAPTAINS, PROVIDING FUNDS FOR THE PAYMENT OF PREMIUMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Expanded Barangay Captains' Insurance Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Expanded Barangay Captains' Insurance Act of 2004\". The barangay, as the basic political unit, plays a significant role in the implementation of government policies, plans and programs. This measure attempts to provide supplemental term insurance coverage to all barangay captains for death, injuries and sickness that may be sustained in the conduct of their official duties and functions. These supplemental benefits are in addition to the insurance coverage being extended to barangay captains by the Government Service Insurance System.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING PRE-SCHOOL EDUCATION, INCREASING THE MONTHLY COMPENSATION OF DAY CARE WORKERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Pre-School Development Act of 2004\". It is the declared policy of the State to provide for a universal early childhood or pre-school education that promotes effective social, intellectual and skills stimulation and value-formation for children from three to five years old with the end in view of preparing them for formal elementary schooling. To implement this policy, this measure aims to institutionalize pre-school education as part of compulsory basic education. The barangay centers shall constitute the public sector pre-school institutions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE AUTOMATIC RETENTION BY THE BARANGAY OF ITS SHARE OF FIFTY PERCENT (50%) IN THE COMMUNITY TAX COLLECTED BY SAID BARANGAY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 164 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Section 164, par (c), subpar (2) of the Local Government Code of 1991 entitles barangay units to share up to fifty percent (50%) of their community tax collection. The section also provides that the share of the national government from the community tax collection shall be remitted by the city or municipality concerned within ten (10) days after the end of each quarter. It is silent as when the barangay shall receive its share of the community taxes. To correct the situation, the bill seeks to amend the provision to allow barangays to automatically retain their fifty percent (50%) share in the community tax collections and to remit the share of the city or municipality within ten (10) days after the end of each month.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2006-12-06

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE TAX ON IDLE LANDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, SECTION 236 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The country has a total land area of 30 million hectares, 47% of which are classified as alienable and disposable. The bill seeks to increase the ceiling tax on idle lands from five percent (5%) to ten percent (10%) to give local government units more flexibility in the imposition of the tax. The current maximum of five percent (5%) has not proven to be deterrent against the non-utilization of agricultural lands for productive purposes. The idle land tax is in addition to the basic real property tax.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 285 AND 286 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, PROVIDING FOR AN EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT (IRA) TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.abstract: The primary objective for distributing internal revene allotment (IRA) to local government units (LGUs) is to lessen the fiscal disparities among urban and rural communities. Unfortunately, the IRA distribution formula under the Local Government Code does not actually address the equity objective. In effect, the well-developed LGUs get bigger IRA shares than those which need them the most. To correct this inequity, the bill proposes to introduce poverty-sensitive factors in the IRA formula in lieu of population, land area and equal sharing. The poverty-sensitive factors are population density, poverty incidence and income class of the LGU. It also allows LGUs to automatically retain their IRA shares.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RE-ALLOCATION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 285 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Under the bill, the allocation of the IRA share shall be made after deducting the cost of devolved responsibilities, including the city-funded hospitals and other legislated benefits such as the Magna Carta for Health Workers and also the salaries of devolved personnel. The proposed reallocation will not only correct the disparity that LGUs suffer from the added cost of maintaining devolved responsibilities but it will erase the apparent mismatch between the allocation of the IRA shares and the distribution of the financial burden as a direct consequence of devolution.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A PROGRAM FOR THE CONTINUING EDUCATION OF COLLEGE TEACHERS, AMENDING FOR SUCH PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7784, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT TO STRENGTHENING TEACHER EDUCATION IN THE PHILIPPINES BY ESTABLISHING CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE, CREATING A TEACHER EDUCATION COUNCIL FOR THE PURPOSE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed bill seeks to institute program for college teachers in both private and public universities and colleges for the purpose of improving the quality of tertiary education in the country by means of upgrading the capability and competence of teachers. The proposed training program shall focus on proper teaching methods and on other areas of study where continuing education is necessary.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL INSURANCE BENEFITS TO ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, PROVIDING FUNDS FOR THE PAYMENT OF ITS PREMIUMS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Public School Teachers' Insurance Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Public School Teachers' Insurance Act of 2004\". Teachers are the single most important factor in education. However, because of their not-so-attractive remuneration, teaching is perceived as a poorly esteemed profession that can not attract the best minds. This bill seeks to improve the plight of teachers by improving the benefits afforded to them to encourage the best minds to join the teaching profession. Specifically, this provides additional insurance benefits to teachers, over and above the benefits given by the Government Service Insurance System.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL BRANCHES, SUBDIVISIONS, INSTRUMENTALITIES, AND AGENCIES OF THE GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS OR THEIR SUBSIDIARIES TO DIVULGE THE IDENTITY OF HIRED FOREIGN CONSULTANTS, THE NATURE OF THEIR WORK AND THEIR COMPENSATION, PERKS AND OTHER PRIVILEGES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES IN CASE OF VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to require full disclosure of the identity, nature or work and compensation of foreign consultants hired or retained by the government, its agencies and instrumentalities including government-owned or controlled corporations. The three main objectives of the bills are: a. to inform the public of the amount being used to pay consultants hired by the government; b. to appraise the public of whether or not the services of these consultants are indispensable and cannot be rendered by our local experts; and c. to enlighten the public of the personalities providing expert advice and support to the government.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2007-02-07

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING BONDS ISSUED BY THE LAND BANK OF THE PHILIPPINES FOR LAND ACQUISITIONS FROM PAYMENT OF THE TWENTY PERCENT (20%) FINAL TAX ON INTEREST INCOME, AMENDING FOR THE SAID PURPOSE SECTION 24 (B)(1) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: In the implementation of the law, the contemplated protection of the just share for the landowners did not actually materialize. In most cases, only the productive portions of the lands were bought, leaving the landowners with unproductive and undesirable portions of the land. To redress a perceived social wrong, this bill proposes to exempt interest earnings on land bank notes paid to landowners from the payment of withholding tax.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SIX HUNDRED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MARINE POLLUTION DECREE OF 1974
rows.abstract: Presidential Decree No. 600 declares as unlawful the throwing, discharge or deposit of any refuse matter of any kind or description. However, the penalty of a fine of five hundred pesos (P500.00) or imprisonment of not more than one (1) year is not at all parallel to the concomitant damage to our waters. This measure seeks to increase the penalty for unlawful dumping and holds the president, manager or director of a corporation or partnership liable for such acts. It sets the guidelines under which dumping may be allowed.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-01-27

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2004-09-15
Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-01-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE AUTOMATIC RELEASE OF THE SHARE OF THE BARANGAY IN THE PROCEEDS OF NATIONAL TAXES AND TAXES ON THE UTILIZATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL WEALTH, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 286, CHAPTER 1 AND SECTION 293, CHAPTER 2, TITLE 3, BOOK II, RESPECTIVELY, OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Under the present system, barangays have to literally beg for their rightful share of the national taxes. To discourage patronage politics and to help attain our goals of decentralization, this measure seeks to provide for the automatic release of the share of the barangays in the national taxes and in taxes imposed on the utilization and development of national wealth.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE COMPETITION COMMISSION, REGULATING AND PENALIZING TRADE PRACTICES THAT LESSEN COMPETITION AND OTHER ANTI-COMPETITIVE PRACTICES AND CONDUCT, UNLAWFUL MERGERS, ACQUISITIONS AND COMBINATIONS IN RESTRAINT OF TRADE, UNFAIR COMPETITION, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Competition Act\".  Competition Law is the primary mechanism in establishing the rules to promote and achieve competitive markets. Its goal is to correct market failure, enhance community welfare, achieve higher economic growth and be competitive in both domestic and international markets. This bill provides for the rules of a competition law and fair trade practices which shall apply to all businesses in the country. It seeks the creation of the Philippine Competition Commission which shall administer the rules on competition.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION OF INVESTMENT COMPANIES
rows.abstract: \"Investment Company Act of 2004\". The measure seeks to amend RA 2629 to provide for a more conducive regulatory environment for the development of investment companies including mutual funds. It also proposes the establishment of the Investment Company Investors Protection Fund which shall compensate investors for financial injury they may suffer due to reasons other than market decline in the investment portfolio of the company.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2005-08-22

rows.author: C102
rows.mother_status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2007-02-05
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROVIDENT PERSONAL SAVINGS PLAN KNOWN AS THE PERSONAL EQUITY AND RETIREMENT ACCOUNT (PERA)
rows.title_short: Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) Act of 2004\". Generally, Filipinos view retirement with trepidation as it means lower or even loss of income because majority of Filipinos do not have retirement benefits to look forward to. This bill seeks to remedy the situation by institutionalizing the Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) for all public and private employees. Under the proposed measure, people will be encouraged to save for their retirement years.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06078

committee_action.action: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2006-09-26
Transmmitted to the Committee on Ways and Means on 2006-11-21

rows.author: C102
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2005-06-01
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PRE-NEED PLAN CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Pre-Need Plan Code of the Philippines
rows.abstract: Concerns have been raised over the pre-need industry's financial status and the protection it affords to investors and pre-need planholders. This bill seeks to establish the legislative framework that will govern the pre-need industry. It sets the industry's regulatory standards with the Securities and Exchange Commission as its regulatory agency. The salient features of the bill include the stipulation of a minimum paid-up capital of PhP 50 million and a margin of solvency of at least PhP 10 million in incorporating a pre-need firm. It also seeks the creation of Liquidity Reserve Fund to protect planholders.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04343

rows.author: C102
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09474) enacted on 2007-05-22
rows.title_full: AN ACT GOVERNING THE ESTABLISHMENT, OPERATION AND REGULATION OF LENDING COMPANIES
rows.title_short: The Lending Company Regulation Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Lending Company Regulation Act of 2004\". In view of the significant impact of lending companies (LCs) in the financial sector, there is an urgent need for a law that would regulate the establishment and activities of LCs to prevent and mitigate practices of LCs that are prejudicial to public interest.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06073
rows.remarks: A similar SB, SB01949, was certified as Urgent by the Pres. on May 30, 2005.

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PROTECTION TO CONSUMERS IN THEIR CREDIT CARD TRANSACTIONS
rows.title_short: Credit Card Consumer Protection Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Credit Card Consumer Protection Act of 2004\". In view of continuing complaints raised against credit card companies for double charging, high interest, penalties, finance and other charges, there is a need to review the issuance of credit cards to protect the interests of consumers. This bill seeks to protect consumders from deceptive price increases for goods and services by prohibiting unfair credit card surcharges. It also aims to encourage the availability of discounts by retailers who wish to offer lower prices for goods and services purchased through the use of credit cards.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2005-01-18, transmitted to on 2005-01-20 and received by the Senate on 2005-01-20
rows.title_full: AN ACT HARMONIZING AND RATIONALIZING THE ADMINISTRATION AND GRANT OF FISCAL AND NON-FISCAL INCENTIVES, REPEALING FOR THIS PURPOSE EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENTS CODE OF 1987
rows.title_short: The Investments and Incentives Code of the Philippines\".
rows.abstract: \"The Investments and Incentives Code of the Philippines\". This bill proposes to extend the maximum period for income tax holiday offered to investors from eight (8) to twelve (12) years subject to certain conditions. The proposed incentive merely tries to align our country's income tax holiday incentive with those granted by our neighboring countries. By matching this incentive with those offered in other countries, we stand an even chance of attracting investments and partners crucial to our development.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03295

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7653, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NEW CENTRAL BANK ACT
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to: a. remove the five-year limit on the Bangko Sentral's tax exemption; b. authorize the Monetary Board (MB) to provide a compensation structure based on job evaluation studies and wage surveys, but not lower than those of  other government financial institutions;  and c. clarify that financial derivatives are subject to the regulation of the MB.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-07-27
rows.remarks: A similar SB, SB01943, was certified as Urgent by the Pres. on May 30, 2005.

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8799, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SECURITIES REGULATION CODE
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend certain provisions of RA 8799, otherwise known as the Securities Regulation Code, in order to promote a more vibrant and healthy capital market. The pertinent provisions, among others, are a) Section 19.1 - ON MANDATORY TENDER OFFERS; b) Section 28.4; (b) - ON MINIMUM CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS; c) Section 30.1 - ON BROKER-DIRECTOR PROHIBITION; and d) Section 33.2 (c) - ON LIMITATION ON OWNERSHIP OF AN EXCHANGE.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER STRENGTHEN CONSUMER PROTECTION BY AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7394, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONSUMER ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to make the National Consumer Affairs Council (NCAC) a truly independent body. By placing the NCAC under the Office of the President, it shall have the power to prepare its annual budget, create other positions necessary to pursue its mandate and assume the authority to represent consumers in their claims and complaints involving violations of the Consumer Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT MODIFYING THE DEFINITION OF A CONDOMINIUM UNIT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4726, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONDOMINIUM LAW TO APPLY TO INDUSTRIAL ESTATES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Condominium Law does not include the industrial estate as a form of a condominium where a single factory, building or plant may comprise a single unit. Said law implicity allows only multi-unit or vertical buildings. This bill seeks to amend the law to include industrial estates in the definition of \"condominium\". This will give investors more flexibility, especially in planning, to enable them to maximize the use of space according to the needs of their operation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RECOVERY OF FINANCIALLY DISTRESSED ENTERPRISES AND THE RESOLUTION OF THEIR INDEBTEDNESS
rows.abstract: \"Corporate Recovery Act\". The bill offers a comprehensive approach to the problems faced by enterprises when they, for whatever reason, can no longer pay their debts as they come due.  It emphasizes on the survival of the enterprise while at the same time keeping paramount the rights of creditors with duly registered liens against the enterprise's assets. It also clarifies the rights of debtors and creditors to initiate formal debt relief proceedings.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2006-01-18
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING ECONOMIC COORDINATION, ADOPTING THE APPROPRIATE MECHANISM THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Economic Coordination Act of 2004\". This bill is anchored on the dictum that economic goal settling should properly involve Congress, the Governor and Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) as well as the National Economic Development Authority headed by the President. It also gives flesh to the mandate of accountability and transparency of the BSP. It specifically sets a feedback loop mechanism on the state of the economy.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04965

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SUBSIDY OVERSIGHT COUNCIL AND PROVIDING THE RULES FOR A RATIONAL MANAGEMENT OF THE GOVERNMENT SUBSIDY SYSTEM
rows.title_short: The Subsidy Oversight Council Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Subsidy Oversight Council Act of 2004\". An important feature of the bill is the creation of the Subsidy Oversight Council that shall serve as a supervisory and recommendatory commission. The Council is tasked to monitor the grant of incentives, government loan guarantees, debt condonation and concessional loans. All government agencies which are empowered to grant subsidies, shall regularly report on such activities to the Council.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2005-08-17

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2005-08-17

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE RULES FOR A COMPETITIVELY NEUTRAL GOVERNMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Despite its policy of privatization and deregulation, the State continues to compete with private enterprises for available economic resources. This bill seeks to establish a competitively neutral government. Competitive neutrality arrangements are intended to minimize resource allocation distortions arising out of public ownership of significant business activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C102
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2006-12-11
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE DRINKING WATER BUSINESSES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Drinking Water Business Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to regulate the business of producing and selling mineral, pure or distilled water. It also protects and safeguards the health of the citizens by insuring that the water they procure and consume are safe to drink as promoted and advertised by drinking water suppliers, distributors or sellers.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05913

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A CHILDREN'S WELFARE FUND FOR THE PROTECTION AND REHABILITATION OF ABANDONED, ABUSED AND SEXUALLY EXPLOITED CHILDREN, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 7610, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SPECIAL PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AGAINST CHILD ABUSE, EXPLOITATION AND DISCRIMINATION ACT
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend RA 7610 by incorporating a Children's Welfate Fund which shall be used exclusively to: a. provide protection and assistance to abandoned or abused or sexually exploited children; b. establish, operate and maintain facilities necessary to rehabilitate such children; c. provide basic education; and d.assist the State in curtailing all forms of child abuse.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D013
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING FURTHER AND BROADENING THE COVERAGE OF THE SPECIAL PROGRAM FOR EMPLOYMENT OF STUDENTS (SPES), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7323
rows.title_short: Strengthening Further and Broadening the Coverage of the Special Program for Employment of Students (SPES)
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to upgrade the provisions Ra 7323 (Poor But Deserving Students Employment Act) by: a. pegging the salary rate of trainees on the minimum wage for private employees and the applicable hiring rate for national and local government agencies; b. indexing the income qualifications for the Special Program for Employment of Students to the annual national poverty threshold line for a family of six to insulate it from legislative amendments every time there is a shift in the poverty line.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-07, transmitted to on 2006-08-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-08-14

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CERTAIN BUILDINGS, INSTITUTIONS, ESTABLISHMENTS AND PUBLIC UTILITIES TO RESERVE SUFFICIENT AND SUITABLE PARKING OR SEATING SPACES FOR THE USE OF EXPECTANT MOTHERS
rows.abstract: Expectant mothers should be given the appropriate care and attention by the State by implementing laws which will help them through the 9 months pregnancy. This bill seeks to require owners of buildings, institutions, establishments and public utilities to reserve sufficient and suitable parking or seating spaces for the use of expectant mothers.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04352

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING HUMAN CLONING IN THE PHILIPPINES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: \"Cloning Prohibition Act of 2001\". Scientific information indicate that cloning, at this point, is not safe to use on humans and that the technique would violate important ethical obligations. The measure seeks to prohibit human cloning in the Philippines, even on an experimental basis. It also provides penalties for violations thereof.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE BEGINNING OF HUMAN LIFE, RECOGNIZING RIGHTS THEREUNDER, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Human Life Act of 2004\". As articulated and intended by the 1986 Constitutional Commission, conception begins with the combination, fusion or integration of the ovum and the sperm cell forming the human nucleus. It also emphasized that the definition of the beginning of human life as from conception shall be provided by an appropriate legislation. This bill seeks to define the beginning of human life and to recognize the rights of the unborn.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL, POLITICAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM ANY AND ALL TAXES THE AMOUNTS AND SIMILAR BENEFITS THAT WILL BE GIVEN TO AND RECEIVED BY HUMAN RIGHTS VICTIMS AS COMPENSATION UNDER THE JUDGE MANUEL REAL DECISION, AND ALL THOSE SIMILARLY SITUATED
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to exempt from any and all kinds of taxes, local or national, any amount of money or similar benefit given to and received by human rights victims as compensation under the decision of Judge Manila Real and those similarly situated. Subjecting such compensation to any form of tax would constitute a travesty of justice for such is not income. At most, such compensation will only be rehabilitative or restorative but it will never approximate the depth and magnitude of the injury or suffering of human rights victims.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCLUSION OF THE MINORITY FLOOR LEADER OF THE SANGGUNIAN CONCERNED IN THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE LOCAL SCHOOL BOARDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The measure seeks to amend Section 98 of the Local Government Code by providing for the inclusion of the Minority Floor Leader of the Sanggunian concerned in the Local School Board (LSB). The Minority in the Sanggunian are the fiscalizers in the disbursement of funds and promulgation of laws in the Sanggunian and their presence in the LSB will give added assurance that the administration of the Special Education Fund will be subjected to scrutiny.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2005-01-12

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING EACH CITY AND MUNICIPALITY TO CREATE A RIVER DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY FOR THE PRESERVATION, PROTECTION, AND DEVELOPMENT OF ALL RIVERS, RIVERSYSTEMS, AND NATURAL WATERWAYS WITHIN ITS RESPECTIVE JURISDICTION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The Philippines had 421 principal rivers and 384 river systems. A great number of these rivers are gradually vanishing, many are dying while others are suffering from physical, biological or chemical damage and some have simply died and vanished. The bill seeks to mandate each city and municipality to create a River Development Authority with the funcitons of preserving, protecting and developing all the rivers, river systems and all natural waterways within their respective jurisdiction.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1069, KNOWN AS THE 'PHILIPPINE EXTRADITION LAW', RATIONALIZING THE EXTRADITION PROCEEDINGS
rows.abstract: The bill stipulates that in the case of a resident Filipino citizen, no warrant of arrest shall be issued before a final determination that such citizen is extraditable. Articles, alleged to have intimate relation to or are the products of the crime for which the accused is sought to be extradited and there is reasonable ground to believe that this is true, may be seized upon order of the court when extradition is granted.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AS NATIONAL POLICY THE FREEDOM OF THE FILIPINO FROM ONEROUS, UNREASONABLE, AND UNCONSCIONABLE DEBT OR OBLIGATION, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 31 (b) OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1177 AND SIMILAR LAWS, DECREES, EXECUTIVE AND ADMINISTRATIVE ORDERS, AND CIRCULARS
rows.abstract: The Filipinos have suffered for long from the burdens of onerous, unreasonable and unconscionable debts and obligation which have eaten up as much as thirty to forty percent of the annual budget as a result of the automatic appropriation provision under Section 31 (b) of PD 1117 and other similar laws, decrees, executive and administrative orders or circulars. This bill seeks to free the Filipino from the burdens of onerous and unreasonable debts by repealing the automatic appropriation provision under PD 1117.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE ALLOCATION FOR THE SPECIAL EDUCATION FUND, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Quality education has taken second place to quantity in our educational system. Elementary and secondary schools, particularly public schools, are operating below standards due inadequate facilities and lack of well-trained educators and classrooms. This bill seeks to double the Special Education Fund in order to give schools the necessary facilities needed by children and to enable teachers to undergo skills upgrading through seminars and training.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to give recognition to the role of micro enterprises which has been tradionally lumped as part of the small enterprise sector. It further seeks to broaden the membership of the Small and Medium Enterprise Development (SMED) Council to include members from the executive and legislative branches. Among other major amendments to RA 6977, it proposes to rename the SMED Council to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development (MSMED) Council.

rows.abstract: Computer education and information technology is the wave sweeping every corner of the globe. In order to raise our competitiveness with our ASEAN neighbors, we should equip our students with the necessary skills in the operation of computers. This bill seeks to require all public high schools to establish and maintain a computer facility that will provide and ensure students access to computers.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PUNISHING THE PILFERAGE OR THEFT OF ANY MATERIAL, PRODUCT, MERCHANDISE, ARTICLE, EQUIPMENT OR BY-PRODUCT MANUFACTURED, PRODUCED, OWNED, OR BELONGING TO INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY ENTERPRISES LOCATED IN SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE
rows.title_short: Anti-Pilferage of Information Technology Materials in Special Economic Zones Act
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Pilferage of Information Technology Materials in Special Economic Zones Act\". Information technology (IT) and related industries have given direct employment to thousands of our countrymen.  Unfortunately, theft and pilferage of this industry's products have been on the rise because of the relative ease in which these products can be taken out because of their miniature size and a high value. The measure seeks to declare as unlawful for any person to tkae, pilfer or steal, with intent to gain, any material, article, equipment or by-products manufactured, produced, owned or belonging to IT enterprises in special economic zones.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A HEAVIER PENALTY AGAINST PUBLIC OFFICERS CHARGED WITH THE CUSTODY OF PRISONERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 223 AND 224 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: The Revised Penal Code punishes offenses committed by public officers who are tasked with the custody of prisoners. However, the penalties provided therein are relatively light. The \"inadequacy\" of the penalty imposed plus the windfall that awaits the jail guard who \"facilitates\" an escape, has led to the \"escape\" of some high-profile criminals. The bill seeks to impose harsher penalties against public officers charged with the custody of prisoners.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05609

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE POLITICAL PARTY SYSTEM AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Political Party Act of 2004\". Reforming campaign finance is one key strategy for fighting corruption in the Philippines. The bill proposes public funding for political parties that demonstrate broad national support as a way of reducing their dependence on interest groups for election campaign contributions. It proposes two sources for public campaign funding: a) a check off from personal and corporate income taxes; and b) a direct allocation from the national budget. Public financing can also be viewed as a way of simplifying and strengthening our party system.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05877

rows.title_full: AN ACT ACCELERATING THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NATIONAL RAILWAY SYSTEM, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL RAILWAY AUTHORITY, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES
rows.abstract: \"National Railways Act\". In order to provide and maintain an adequate, efficient, inexpensive, convenient and reliable public transport system responsive to the needs of the citizenry, this bill provides for the creation the National Railway Authority which shall formulate and adopt a comprehensive development plan for a national railway system that meets ecological and environmental standards. It shall promote and encourage the active participation of the private sector, both local and international, in the development and implementation of a comprehensive development plan for a railway system.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RAILWAYS AND RO-RO SYSTEMS since 2006-05-30

rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09485) enacted on 2007-06-02
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPROVING THE EFFICIENCY IN THE DELIVERY OF GOVERNMENT SERVICES TO THE PUBLIC BY REDUCING BUREAUCRATIC RED TAPE AND PREVENTING GRAFT AND CORRUPTION
rows.abstract: \"Red Tape Reduction Act of 2004\". Bureaucratic red tape does not only lengthen the procedure in securing vital government services but it also opens avenues for bribery and corruption. The bill provides a maximum of fifteen and thirty working days for concerned government agencies to act on simple and complex transactions, respectively. It limits the number of signatories to the officers and employees directly supervising the specific unit where a particular transaction is being acted upon. It also institutionalizes a Report Card Survey that shall assess the performance of the different agencies.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03776

committee_action.remarks: approved on third reading

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REENGINEER THE GOVERNMENT BUREAUCRACY BY AUTHORIZING THE PRESIDENT TO IMPLEMENT THE RE-ENGINEERING PLAN, CREATING THE COMMISSION ON GOVERNMENT RE-ENGINEERING AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"The Re-Engineering Act of 2004\". The government bureucracy has become unwieldy and corruption-ridden. The bill proposes for a multi-year process of bureaucratic re-engineering to allow for thorough studies and consultation . Civil servants in agencies deemed non-vital shall be offered a attractive gratuity package. Employees of such agencies who wish to remain in government may be re-assigned to other surviving entities. On the other hand, agencies deemed important will have the option to undertake the gratuity package for not more than 20% of their employees.
rows.status: Transmitted to the Committee on Appropriations on 2006-02-01

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 141, 142, 143, 144 AND 145 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to increase the existing excise tax rate on tobacco and alcohol products or \"sin products\" and to index the same to inflation. It further proposes the removal of the codal classification of excisable products by brand. The passage of the bill is expected to generate at least PhP 4 billion in the first year of implementation.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03174

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL ALLOWABLE TAX DEDUCTIONS FOR INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 34 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: The increasing cost of rentals on dwellings has forced countless families to scrimp on other basic necessities. Many have resorted to becoming informal settlers, turning blind eyes to the dangers posed to their children in such communities. This bill seeks to provide some measure of relief to our taxpayers who are married or heads of their families, by including their rentals as allowable deductions from their gross income. It is envisioned that the said amount shall be used to provide for other equally important needs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE MARITIME AND OCEAN AFFAIRS CENTER AS AN ATTACHED AGENCY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS, PROVIDING FOR ITS FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Maritime and Ocean Affairs Center Act of 2002\". The State recognizes that marine resources and environment, including those of the oceans, all seas, archipelagic waters and adjacent coastal areas, form an integrated whole that are essential components of the national ocean economy and life-support system vital to sustainable development. This measure seeks the creation of the Maritime and Ocean Affairs Center (MOAC) which shall serve as the secretariat to the Department of Foreign Affairs on maritime and ocean affairs matters. Among its other functions, the MOAC shall initiate steps to harmonize and update domestic legislation and rules and regulations with international agreements to which the Philippines is a party.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-08-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY COUNCIL, PROVIDING POWERS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Emergency Health Powers Act\". It is imperative that a plan of action be established to counteract the emergence of contagions like SARS (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome). The need is made even more urgent with the threat of a deliberate outbreak via bioterrosm. The bill seeks to establish a Public Health Emergency Council which shall draw up a battle plan against public health emergencies and to implement the same. It aims to give us a fighting chance against biological, chemical or nuclear health treats through preparation, management and disposal.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING LOCAL HOUSING BOARDS IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY, PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Local Housing Boards Act\". The problem of shelter is one that is shared by almost all municipalities and cities in the country. Because it is basic need, it is imperative that government exerts a concentrated effort to find solutions to the shelter problem. The bill seeks to institutionalize Local Housing Boards which will be created at the level of local government units (LGUs). The LGUs are in the best position to know the peculiarities of their locality and establish their priorities. Local housing boards shall be responsible for the formulation of a housing program in their respective areas of jurisdiction.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03769

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A SOCIALIZED AND LOW-COST HOUSING LOAN RESTRUCTURING PROGRAM, PROVIDING THE MECHANISMS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Socialized and Low-Cost Housing Loan Restructuring Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Socialized and Low-Cost Housing Loan Restructuring Act of 2003\". The Asian crisis of 1997 affected many Filipinos including those who availed of low-cost and socialized housing offered on a supply-dictated basis at the behest of the Ramos administration. Despite the enactment of RA 8501 to remedy the problem of unpaid mortgages and defaulting housing loan borrowers, only 19,000 out 180,000 defaulting accounts availed of the condonation program. The bill seeks to provide fresh hope to those who failed to avail of the provisions of RA 8501 but wish to keep their homes and pay their loans at rates affordable and in keeping with their current economic status.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03835

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TRAVEL ALLOWANCES TO BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7883, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'THE BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS' BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES ACT OF 1995,' AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend Section 6 of RA 7883 by granting travel allowances to barangay health workers to aid in the fulfillment of their duties. The token amount can help defray the cost of transportation incurred in the performance of their duties. More importantaly, it will also exhibit the government's appreciation of their heroic efforts.
